results.primary_cause: Exact, current evidence confirming or contradicting the container spot/contract freight and liner-utilization cycle was insufficient; the available peer-oriented result did not establish industry freight-rate or utilization causality.

Evidence confirms recent Capesize freight-rate strength, but counter-evidence indicates that 2026 strength may be substantially driven by temporary Hormuz rerouting and could reverse into a 2027 supply glut; the exact durability and breadth of the BDI/Capesize/Panamax commodity-volume cycle remain unresolved.

supporting_evidence.claim: A key dry-bulk shipping-rate measure reached its highest level since December 2023, driven by rising Capesize demand and tightening vessel supply.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand

counter_evidence.claim: BIMCO warned that apparent 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially artificial because of forced Hormuz rerouting and could reverse into a 2027 supply glut.
counter_evidence.source_title: Dry bulk shipping faces 2027 supply glut: BIMCO warns Hormuz rerouting boost will reverse

results.primary_cause: Exact current evidence on mature- and specialty-node utilization, wafer pricing, customer inventory, and end-demand was insufficient; leading-edge AI/HPC evidence cannot confirm this driver.
